title: p95 Latency Statistical Equivalence and Tail Distribution Audit
methodology: Quantile estimation under clustered repeated measures (M=12 specimen clusters, K=5 blocks, nominal N=60 per condition)

normal_vs_disabled.operational_impact: Non-monument and borderline specimens traverse the uncertainty logging and exception ticketing pathways, where background thread pool dispatch induces modest additional tail scheduling latency on pure CPU.

slow_vs_disabled.operational_impact: Simulated 550ms worker tasks trigger cooperative deadline checks, causing background workers to remain busy up to the 500ms deadline, mildly amplifying tail CPU contention for concurrent outlier queries.

saturated_vs_disabled.operational_impact: Under queue saturation, excess shadow tasks are rejected immediately via SHADOW_SKIPPED_CAPACITY in O(1) time without thread dispatch, keeping p95 within 36ms of baseline. However, wide clustered confidence intervals prevent formal equivalence declaration.

summary_findings.primary_cause: Bimodal latency profile between clean catalog queries (~180ms) and exception logging queries (~1400ms), compounded by limited independent specimen clusters (M=12).
summary_findings.recommendation: Maintain controlled staging; gather expanded specimen dataset (M >= 150) before re-evaluating tail equivalence.
